name: ADU Cost per Square Foot in Los Angeles County in 2026: What Drives the Range?

mainEntity.name: What are realistic per‑square‑foot cost ranges for different types of ADUs in Los Angeles County in 2026, and which factors cause the biggest swings?
mainEntity.text: What are realistic per‑square‑foot cost ranges for different types of ADUs in Los Angeles County in 2026, and which factors cause the biggest swings?

acceptedAnswer.text: By 2026, ADU costs in Los Angeles County vary widely depending on type and site conditions, so per‑square‑foot numbers should be treated as broad ranges rather than precise quotes. Straightforward garage conversions with minimal structural changes and simple finishes tend to fall at the lower end of the spectrum, while new, detached ADUs with full kitchens, high ceilings, and private outdoor spaces sit in mid to high ranges. Projects in hillside or fire zones, or those requiring extensive grading, retaining walls, or utility upgrades, often land at the top of the range—or beyond. The biggest cost swings come from site and structure rather than interior finishes alone. Poor access that requires hand‑carrying materials, tight urban lots that complicate staging, or older garages needing new slabs and framing can all drive up labor. Utility upgrades, such as new panels, long trench runs, or separate meters, are another major variable. On the finish side, moving from basic to high‑end cabinetry, tile, and fixtures can significantly raise costs, but these can be adjusted to match your budget more easily than foundation or framing. When comparing bids, insist on itemized scopes that separate site work, utilities, structure, interiors, and soft costs. This allows you to understand why one contractor’s per‑square‑foot price is higher and where you can reduce scope without compromising safety or long‑term durability.
